stem: If P(n, 3) = 60, what is the value of n?

per_option_rationale.rationale: P(n, 3) = n(n-1)(n-2) = 60. Try n = 5: 5 x 4 x 3 = 60. Confirmed.
Chose n = 6, but P(6, 3) = 6 x 5 x 4 = 120 which is not 60. Off by one in the candidate value.
Chose n = 4, but P(4, 3) = 4 x 3 x 2 = 24 which is not 60. Off by one in the other direction.
Chose n = 7, perhaps computing 60 / 3 = 20 and misidentifying the cube root or misreading the descending product starting from 7.

explanation: P(n, 3) = n(n-1)(n-2) = 60. Factoring 60 = 5 x 4 x 3, three consecutive descending integers from 5. Therefore n = 5.

explanation_sections.punchline: Factor 60 as a product of three consecutive descending integers: 5 x 4 x 3 = 60, so n = 5.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify as back-solving a permutation equation. Write P(n, 3) = n(n-1)(n-2) = 60. Trial n = 5: 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 checks out. Alternatively, note 60^(1/3) approx 3.9, so n is around 5, then verify.
explanation_sections.lesson: To back-solve P(n, r) = k, factor k as r consecutive descending integers. The largest integer is n.
explanation_sections.timing: 50-60 s. Check n = 5 first since 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 is a well-known product. Trap is testing n = 6 giving 120, which is double 60 - a common off-by-one check.
